name: microagi
status: active public company presence; legal registry status not independently checked
product: Atlas scopes factory work, selects model and hardware, recreates and trains the workstation off-site, validates safety and deploys the working system as a managed rental; Shift captures human work as training-ready data.
mission: Deploy embodied intelligence into industrial operations and turn deployment data into compounding robotics research.
customerProblem: Close the gap between capable robot hardware and models and a reliable robot performing a specific production task.
workflow: on-site workflow capture; feasibility study; hardware and model selection; workstation reconstruction; policy fine-tuning; failure testing; commissioning; managed production operation
initialTargetCustomer: European industrial manufacturers with manual production workflows
economicBuyer: Manufacturing operations and automation leadership; exact purchasing authority and budget were not publicly verified.
currentScope: Company and investor sources describe workstation-level factory deployment and managed rental; no customer-controlled deployment evidence was identified.
ambitionScope: A hardware- and model-agnostic deployment layer for industrial robotics, backed by a reusable physical-work dataset and European data sovereignty.
businessModel: Investor states microagi buys the hardware and rents the working system, with payment aligned to operation; exact pricing, SLA and contract terms were not independently verified.
goToMarket: Direct enterprise motion using on-site scoping and forward-deployed engineers; named channel arrangements were not verified.
namedCustomers: The company claims deployment into major industrial operations, but no customer-controlled named production deployment was identified in the reviewed public sources.
fundingNote: One source-checked USD financing event; not total funding or a complete round history.
fundingRaw: $55M seed led by Hummingbird Ventures, with Redalpine, Northzone, LocalGlobe and Village Global participating
thesis: Evidence-bounded thesis: microagi positions Atlas as the prime deployment layer between third-party robot hardware and frontier models. Public company and investor evidence supports workflow capture, off-site cell reconstruction, policy adaptation, safety testing, integration, commissioning, hardware-risk absorption and managed rental. It does not establish customer-controlled production performance, uptime, pricing, margins or declining engineering hours across repeated deployments. Alexandria and Shift are presented as the reusable data assets, but cross-customer transfer and legal compounding remain unverified.
relevanceToIntegration: Direct integration comparator: public evidence says microagi scopes the task, selects hardware and models, reconstructs the workstation, trains and tests the system, deploys it on the line and rents the working result. Independent customer acceptance and operating economics remain unverified.
evidenceGaps: Customer-controlled deployment confirmation; named production site; acceptance criteria; uptime/SLA; remote-intervention boundary; exact pricing and contract risk; realised gross margin; cross-deployment engineering decline; data-rights and cross-customer learning remain unverified.
